newsitem.title: UK: Licht sees 1996/97 coffee output sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Licht sees 1996/97 coffee output sharply higher.

text.p: World coffee production should reach 97.7 million bags in 1996/97, sharply up on the 1995/96 figure of 87.7 million bags and largely due to a recovery in Brazil's crop, statistician F.O. Licht said on Friday.
Robusta production would account for 32.2 million bags and arabica for 65.5 million, Licht said in its first estimate of the 1996/97 world coffee balance.

"The increase largely reflects the recovery in Brazil after drought and frost damaged the 1995/96 crop, but better husbandry after higher producer prices in recent years also played its role," it said.
Coffee production in South America was forecast at 43.2 million bags, significantly higher than last year's figure of 33.4 million bags.
Brazilian output was, as usual, the continent's highest and estimated at between 26 and 27 million bags -- a dramatic recovery from the previous year's weather-damaged crop of 15.8 million bags.
World coffee exports would amount to 76.1 million bags in 1996/97 after 70.2 million the previous year, it said.
Licht forecast Asian coffee production at 17.1 million bags of which Indonesia was expected to provide up to 8.0 million.

Ivory Coast would dominate African production in 1996/97 and was likely to turn out a record production of between 4.2 and 5.0 million bags, compared with a total figure for Africa of around 18 million bags.
North and Central America would probably produce a little less coffee in 1996/97 with output expected to reach 18.1 million bags and Mexico as the leading producer.
